title: provide and inject: the escape hatch and what it costs

videos.script:
Some values are needed everywhere. A unit, a language, a lookup of course titles. Passing them down as props means every component in between carries something it never uses. {{drilling}} That is called prop drilling, and you will see it in its smallest form first.

{{provide}} Vue's answer is provide and inject. A component provides a value under a key, and any component below it, at any depth, injects it. The ones in between are left out.

{{readonly}} A value that changes is provided as a ref. You will provide one read-only, with a function beside it, and watch a direct write be refused.

{{keys}} Then why the key should be a Symbol, not a string. {{missing}} Then what happens when nobody provides anything, and how to choose a default that does not hide the problem.

{{cost}} And then the price. A component that injects no longer shows what it needs. The planner pays it once, for its course titles, and you will see why it pays it there and nowhere else.
